human_result: FAILED — opened in Adobe Illustrator as one solid black silhouette
screenshot_note: the owner reported the black result in writing; no screenshot file was supplied to this environment, so none is claimed as held
prolog_note: the prolog was empty, so no AI operator had any PostScript definition; the file could not render outside Illustrator and its colour could not be checked by execution at all

root_cause.finding: the AI source and the PDF proof were written by two different, unshared implementations, and only the PDF's was ever inspected
evidence: the accepted PDF proof committed in the same commit carries the four correct colours as PDF `rg`/`RG` operators
the accepted PNG proof rasterises those same four colours
the same commit's .ai carries 0.0000 0.0000 0.0000 Xa for all 40 objects
no emitter for the .ai exists anywhere in the repository, so the colour it should have written was never in tested code
root_cause.mechanism: the AI writer emitted a constant zero RGB triple in place of each object's colour. Because %%DocumentProcessColors declared Black only, the resulting file was internally consistent and looked plausible as text.
root_cause.why_it_was_not_caught: the reviewed artefacts were the PDF and PNG, which were correct; the .ai was checked for structure, object count and geometry, none of which reads colour

second_divergence.finding: the AI declared no stroke width for the divider, so it would draw at the PostScript default 1 pt while the accepted proof strokes it at 0.362384 pt
second_divergence.source_of_value: read from the accepted PDF proof's content stream, not chosen here

root_cause.fix: one object/colour model now emits the AI, the PDF and the PNG; colour is written from the object's role at emission time and an unassigned colour raises instead of defaulting to black
